claim: Multivalent presentation of viral glycoproteins can substantially increase the elicitation of antigen-specific antibodies.
source: Multivalent presentation of viral glycoproteins can substantially increase the elicitation of antigen-specific antibodies.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the abstract supported by the broader scientific literature on multivalent antigen presentation.

claim: Self-assembling protein nanoparticles were designed with geometries tailored to present the ectodomains of influenza, HIV, and RSV viral glycoprotein trimers.
source: We first de novo designed trimers tailored for antigen fusion, featuring N-terminal helices positioned to match the C termini of the viral glycoproteins.
evidence: The manuscript describes the computational design and experimental validation of nanoparticles for these three viral antigens.

claim: Trimers were designed featuring N-terminal helices positioned to match the C termini of viral glycoproteins.
source: We first de novo designed trimers tailored for antigen fusion, featuring N-terminal helices positioned to match the C termini of the viral glycoproteins.
evidence: This design strategy is explicitly stated and shown in Figure 1.

claim: Trimers that experimentally adopted their designed configurations were incorporated as components of tetrahedral, octahedral, and icosahedral nanoparticles.
source: Trimers that experimentally adopted their designed configurations were incorporated as components of tetrahedral, octahedral, and icosahedral nanoparticles, which were characterized by cryo-electron microscopy and assessed for their ability to present viral glycoproteins.
evidence: The manuscript presents experimental characterization data including cryo-EM structures for nanoparticles with these symmetries.

claim: The designed nanoparticles presented antigenically intact prefusion HIV-1 Env, influenza hemagglutinin, and RSV F trimers in the predicted geometries.
source: Electron microscopy and antibody binding experiments demonstrated that the designed nanoparticles presented antigenically intact prefusion HIV-1 Env, influenza hemagglutinin, and RSV F trimers in the predicted geometries.
evidence: This is supported by EM data in Figures 5 and antibody binding data in Figure 5 supplements and Figure 6.

claim: Multivalent antigen presentation increases cross-linking of antigen-specific B cell receptors at the cell surface.
source: This has been attributed to increased cross-linking of antigen-specific B cell receptors at the cell surface and modulation of immunogen trafficking to and within lymph nodes (Irvine et al., 2013; Tokatlian et al., 2019).
evidence: This mechanism is cited from published literature.

claim: Multivalent antigen presentation modulates immunogen trafficking to and within lymph nodes.
source: This has been attributed to increased cross-linking of antigen-specific B cell receptors at the cell surface and modulation of immunogen trafficking to and within lymph nodes (Irvine et al., 2013; Tokatlian et al., 2019).
evidence: This mechanism is cited from published literature.

claim: Complex oligomeric or engineered antigens are difficult to stably incorporate into non-protein-based nanomaterials.
source: An ongoing challenge has been to develop multimerization scaffolds capable of presenting complex oligomeric or engineered antigens (Sanders and Moore, 2017; Jardine et al., 2013; McLellan et al., 2013a), as these can be difficult to stably incorporate into non-protein-based nanomaterials (e.g. liposomes, polymers, transition metals and their oxides).
evidence: This is stated as a known challenge in the field with supporting citations.

claim: Self-assembling ferritin nanoparticles have been used to present complex oligomeric antigens.
source: Several reports have utilized non-viral, naturally occurring protein scaffolds, such as self-assembling ferritin (Kanekiyo et al., 2013; Sliepen et al., 2015; Darricarrère et al., 2018), lumazine synthase (Sanders and Moore, 2017; Abbott et al., 2018), or encapsulin (Kanekiyo et al., 2015) nanoparticles, to present a variety of complex oligomeric or engineered antigens.
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published work.

claim: Self-assembling proteins as scaffolds for antigen presentation provide enhanced immunogenicity.
source: These studies have illustrated the advantages of using self-assembling proteins as scaffolds for antigen presentation (López-Sagaseta et al., 2016; Kanekiyo et al., 2019), including enhanced immunogenicity and seamless integration of antigen and scaffold through genetic fusion.
evidence: This advantage is cited from published literature.

claim: Computationally designed protein nanoparticles confer high stability, robust assembly, ease of production and purification, and increased potency upon immunization.
source: More recently, computationally designed one- and two-component protein nanoparticles (Hsia et al., 2016; King et al., 2014; Bale et al., 2016) have been used to present complex oligomeric antigens, conferring additional advantages such as high stability, robust assembly, ease of production and purification, and increased potency upon immunization (Marcandalli et al., 2019; Brouwer et al., 2019).
evidence: These advantages are cited from published work on designed nanoparticles.

claim: A close geometric match between the C termini of the antigen and the N termini of a designed nanoparticle component would enable multivalent presentation without structural distortion near the glycoprotein base.
source: For homo-oligomeric class I viral fusion proteins, a large group that includes many important vaccine antigens (Harrison, 2015), a close geometric match between the C termini of the antigen and the N termini of a designed nanoparticle component would enable multivalent presentation without structural distortion near the glycoprotein base, and potentially allow for better retention of antigenic epitopes relevant to protection.
evidence: This is a design rationale stated in the introduction.

claim: Monomeric repeat proteins were docked into C3-symmetric trimers using the RPX docking method.
source: They were docked into C3-symmetric trimers using our RPX docking method, which identifies configurations likely to accommodate favorable side chain packing at the de novo designed interface (Fallas et al., 2017).
evidence: This computational method is described in the Results section.

claim: Twenty-three trimer designs were selected for experimental characterization.
source: Geometrically compatible docks (non-clashing termini separation distances of 15 Å or less) were subjected to full Rosetta C3-symmetric interface design and filtering (see Materials and Methods), and twenty-three designs were selected for experimental characterization (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to a figure.

claim: Twenty-two of the designed trimers expressed in the soluble fraction.
source: Twenty-two designs were found to express in the soluble fraction, and nine formed the intended trimeric oligomerization state as assessed by SEC in tandem with multi-angle light scattering (SEC-MALS; examples in Figure 2 top panel, second row; SEC-MALS chromatograms for the remaining designs are in Figure 2—figure supplement 2 and data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1—source data 1; SEC chromatograms for remaining designs with off-target retention volumes are in Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This experimental result is reported with supporting data in figures.

claim: Nine designed trimers formed the intended trimeric oligomerization state as assessed by SEC-MALS.
source: Twenty-two designs were found to express in the soluble fraction, and nine formed the intended trimeric oligomerization state as assessed by SEC in tandem with multi-angle light scattering (SEC-MALS; examples in Figure 2 top panel, second row; SEC-MALS chromatograms for the remaining designs are in Figure 2—figure supplement 2 and data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1—source data 1; SEC chromatograms for remaining designs with off-target retention volumes are in Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This experimental result is reported with supporting data in figures.

claim: Design 1na0C3_2 exhibited a backbone r.m.s.d. between the design model and crystal structure of 1.4 Å.
source: Structures were determined at resolutions of 2.6 and 2.3 Å, revealing a backbone root mean square deviation (r.m.s.d.) between the design model and structure of 1.4 and 0.8 Å, respectively (Figure 2—figure supplement 3, and Figure 2—figure supplement 3—source data 1, crystallization conditions, structure metrics, and structure-to-model comparisons are described in Materials and Methods).
evidence: This structural validation is reported with crystallographic data.

claim: Design 3ltjC3_1v2 exhibited a backbone r.m.s.d. between the design model and crystal structure of 0.8 Å.
source: Structures were determined at resolutions of 2.6 and 2.3 Å, revealing a backbone root mean square deviation (r.m.s.d.) between the design model and structure of 1.4 and 0.8 Å, respectively (Figure 2—figure supplement 3, and Figure 2—figure supplement 3—source data 1, crystallization conditions, structure metrics, and structure-to-model comparisons are described in Materials and Methods).
evidence: This structural validation is reported with crystallographic data.

claim: The crystal structures confirmed that the designed proteins adopt the intended trimeric configurations.
source: The structures confirmed in both cases that the designed proteins adopt the intended trimeric configurations, and that most of the atomic details at the de novo designed interfaces are recapitulated.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the crystal structure analysis.

claim: Fifty-three nanoparticle designs across all three targeted symmetries were selected for experimental characterization.
source: Fifty-three nanoparticle designs across all three targeted symmetries that exhibited the best interface metrics were selected for experimental characterization (see Materials and Methods).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the nanoparticle design process.

claim: Twenty-four of the nanoparticle designs showed pairs of proteins at the expected molecular weights co-eluting by SDS-PAGE.
source: Pairs of proteins at the expected molecular weights were found to co-elute by SDS-PAGE for twenty-four of the designs, consistent with spontaneous assembly of the nanoparticles followed by pulldown His6-tagged component (featured co-eluting designs are presented in Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This experimental result is reported with supporting gel data.

claim: Five nanoparticle designs ran as monodisperse particles of the predicted molecular mass by SEC-MALS.
source: Five designs comprising a panel of unique geometric configurations, T33_dn2, T33_dn5, T33_dn10, O43_dn18, and I53_dn5, ran as monodisperse particles of the predicted molecular mass by SEC-MALS and were further investigated by SAXS.
evidence: This experimental result is reported with supporting data in Figure 2.

claim: The experimental solution scattering curves closely matched the scattering curves computed from the design models for T33_dn2, T33_dn5, T33_dn10, O43_dn18, and I53_dn5.
source: The experimental solution scattering curves closely matched the scattering curves computed from the design models (Schneidman-Duhovny et al., 2010) for all five designs (Figure 2, bottom panel and Figure 2—figure supplement 6; metrics in Table 1 and Figure 2—source data 1, bottom five designs).
evidence: This SAXS validation is shown in Figure 2 with quantitative metrics.

claim: The two components of I53_dn5 can be separately produced and assembled in vitro.
source: Due to its high valency and production yield, we selected the I53_dn5 nanoparticle to investigate the capacity of its two components to be separately produced and assembled in vitro.
evidence: This capability is demonstrated experimentally in Figure 2—figure supplement 7.

claim: Nanoparticle assembly of I53_dn5 appeared to be complete within minutes after equimolar mixing of components.
source: Nanoparticle assembly appeared to be complete within minutes after equimolar mixing (Figure 2—figure supplement 7).
evidence: This observation is reported with supporting SEC data.

claim: NS-EM analysis confirmed high sample homogeneity for all five nanoparticle designs.
source: Analysis of the NS-EM data confirmed high sample homogeneity for all five nanoparticle designs as evident from the micrographs and 2D class-averages (Figure 3).
evidence: This is shown in the NS-EM images and 2D class averages in Figure 3.

claim: All five nanoparticles assemble as predicted by the design models, at least to the resolution limits of NS-EM.
source: While some free nanoparticle components were detected in the T33_dn5 sample, suggesting a certain propensity towards disassembly, analysis of the reconstructed 3D maps revealed that all five nanoparticles assemble as predicted by the design models, at least to the resolution limits of NS-EM.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from NS-EM 3D reconstructions shown in Figure 3.

claim: The final resolutions of the cryo-EM reconstructed maps were 3.9, 4.5, and 5.3 Å for T33_dn10, O43_dn18, and I53_dn5, respectively.
source: The final resolutions of the reconstructed maps for the T33_dn10, O43_dn18, and I53_dn5 nanoparticles were 3.9, 4.5, and 5.3 Å, respectively.
evidence: These resolution values are reported from cryo-EM data processing.

claim: Some structural heterogeneity was observed in the cryo-EM data, particularly in the case of I53_dn5.
source: Some structural heterogeneity was observed in the cryo-EM data, particularly in the case of I53_dn5.
evidence: This observation is noted from the cryo-EM data analysis.

claim: Backbone r.m.s.d. values for the asymmetric unit were 0.65, 0.98, and 1.3 Å for T33_dn10, O43_dn18, and I53_dn5, respectively.
source: Backbone r.m.s.d. values estimated for the asymmetric unit (consisting of a single subunit of component A and component B) were 0.65, 0.98, and 1.3 Å for T33_dn10, O43_dn18, and I53_dn5, respectively (Table 1).
evidence: These values are calculated from the refined cryo-EM structures compared to design models.

claim: BG505 SOSIP trimers are clearly discernible in 2D class-averages and reconstructed 3D maps of antigen-displaying nanoparticles.
source: BG505 SOSIP trimers are clearly discernible in 2D class-averages and reconstructed 3D maps.
evidence: This is shown in the NS-EM data in Figure 5.

claim: The trimers appear less well-resolved than the corresponding nanoparticle core in the three reconstructions, likely due to the short flexible linkers between the BG505 SOSIP trimer and the fusion component.
source: However, the trimers appear less well-resolved than the corresponding nanoparticle core in the three reconstructions, likely due to the short flexible linkers between the BG505 SOSIP trimer and the fusion component.
evidence: This observation is made from the NS-EM reconstructions with a proposed explanation.

claim: Fusion of the BG505 SOSIP trimer did not induce any major structural changes to the underlying nanoparticle scaffolds.
source: The self-assembling cores of the antigen-fused T33_dn2, T33_dn10, and I53_dn5 nanoparticles were very similar to the NS-EM maps of the unmodified nanoparticles (at least to the resolution limits of NS-EM), demonstrating that fusion of the BG505 SOSIP trimer did not induce any major structural changes to the underlying nanoparticle scaffolds.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from comparison of NS-EM maps with and without antigen.

claim: Free components were detected in raw EM micrographs of BG505 SOSIP–I53_dn5, indicating some degree of disassembly.
source: Free components were detected in raw EM micrographs of BG505 SOSIP–I53_dn5, indicating some degree of disassembly.
evidence: This observation is made from the NS-EM micrographs.

claim: BG505 SOSIP–I53_dn5 demonstrated sensitivity to various physical and chemical stressors.
source: This finding is supported by stability data reported in a parallel study, where BG505 SOSIP–I53_dn5 demonstrated sensitivity to various physical and chemical stressors (Antanasijevic et al., 2020).
evidence: This is cited from a parallel study.

claim: DS-Cav1–I53_dn5 nanoparticle binds the RSV F-specific mAbs D25, Motavizumab, and AM14 similarly to soluble DS-Cav1 trimer with foldon.
source: The DS-Cav1–I53_dn5 nanoparticle was found by an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) to bind the RSV F-specific mAbs D25 (McLellan et al., 2013b), Motavizumab (Cingoz, 2009), and AM14 (Gilman et al., 2015) similarly to soluble DS-Cav1 trimer with foldon (McLellan et al., 2013a), indicating that the F protein is presented in the desired prefusion conformation on the nanoparticle (Figure 4—figure supplement 1, top).
evidence: This is demonstrated by ELISA data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The F protein is presented in the desired prefusion conformation on the DS-Cav1–I53_dn5 nanoparticle.
source: The DS-Cav1–I53_dn5 nanoparticle was found by an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) to bind the RSV F-specific mAbs D25 (McLellan et al., 2013b), Motavizumab (Cingoz, 2009), and AM14 (Gilman et al., 2015) similarly to soluble DS-Cav1 trimer with foldon (McLellan et al., 2013a), indicating that the F protein is presented in the desired prefusion conformation on the nanoparticle (Figure 4—figure supplement 1, top).
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the antibody binding data.

claim: Both the HA–I53_dn5 nanoparticle and the HA–I53_dn5B trimer presented the head and stem regions with wild-type-like antigenicity.
source: Biolayer interferometry binding experiments with anti-HA head - and stem-specific mAbs (Krause et al., 2011; Ekiert et al., 2009) analogously showed that both the HA–I53_dn5 nanoparticle and the HA–I53_dn5B trimer presented the head and stem regions with wild-type-like antigenicity (Figure 5—figure supplement 2, top).
evidence: This is demonstrated by biolayer interferometry data in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: Antigen crowding can modulate the accessibility of specific epitopes on HIV-1 Env trimers presented on icosahedral nanoparticle scaffolds.
source: Previous work involving icosahedral nanoparticle scaffolds presenting HIV-1 Env trimers has shown that antigen crowding can modulate the accessibility of specific epitopes and thereby influence the humoral immune response (Brouwer et al., 2019; Brinkkemper and Sliepen, 2019).
evidence: This is cited from previous published work.

claim: BG505 SOSIP–T33_dn2 presents four copies of the BG505 SOSIP trimer with much greater spacing than BG505 SOSIP–I53-50 with twenty copies.
source: BG505 SOSIP–T33_dn2 presents four copies of the BG505 SOSIP trimer with much greater spacing than BG505 SOSIP–I53-50 with twenty copies.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the epitope accessibility experiments.

claim: The difference in spacing between BG505 trimers on T33_dn2 and I53-50 derives from the angles between neighboring three-fold rotational symmetry axes in icosahedral and tetrahedral point group symmetries (41.8° and 109.5°, respectively).
source: This difference derives from the angles between neighboring three-fold rotational symmetry axes—where the displayed BG505 trimers are located on the nanoparticle surfaces—in icosahedral and tetrahedral point group symmetries (41.8° and 109.5°, respectively).
evidence: This is a geometric calculation based on the symmetry properties.

claim: For mAbs that target apical, V3-base, and CD4-binding site epitopes (PGT145, PGT122, 2G12, and VRC01), the number of molecules of trimer or nanoparticle bound was relatively similar (ratio ~ 1).
source: For mAbs that target apical, V3-base, and CD4-binding site epitopes (PGT145, PGT122, 2G12, and VRC01) (Gilman et al., 2015; Walker et al., 2011; Trkola et al., 1996; Wu et al., 2010), the number of molecules of trimer or nanoparticle bound was relatively similar (ratio ~ 1).
evidence: This result is from SPR experiments shown in Figure 6.

claim: For mAbs that target more base-proximate epitopes in the gp120-gp41 interface (ACS202, VRC34, and PGT151), an inter-protomeric gp41 epitope (3BC315), and the main autologous neutralizing antibody epitope in the glycan hole centered on residues 241 and 289 (11B), the accessibility was reduced in the nanoparticle format.
source: However, for mAbs that target more base-proximate epitopes in the gp120-gp41 interface (ACS202, VRC34, and PGT151) (van Gils et al., 2017; Kong et al., 2016; Falkowska et al., 2014), an inter-protomeric gp41 epitope (3BC315) (Klein et al., 2012), and the main autologous neutralizing antibody epitope in the glycan hole centered on residues 241 and 289 (11B) (McCoy et al., 2016), the accessibility was reduced in the nanoparticle format.
evidence: This result is from SPR experiments shown in Figure 6.

claim: Binding to a mAb directed to the trimer base (12N) was not observed for nanoparticle BG505 SOSIP–T33_dn2.
source: Binding to a mAb directed to the trimer base (12N) (McCoy et al., 2016) was not observed for nanoparticle BG505 SOSIP–T33_dn2 (Figure 6b).
evidence: This result is from SPR experiments shown in Figure 6.

claim: For mAbs that target the more base-proximate epitopes in the gp120-gp41 interface (VRC34 and PGT151), there was nearly three-fold higher epitope accessibility on T33_dn2 compared to I53-50.
source: However, for mAbs that target the more base-proximate epitopes in the gp120-gp41 interface (VRC34 and PGT151), there was nearly three-fold higher epitope accessibility on T33_dn2 compared to I53-50 (Figure 6c).
evidence: This result is from comparative SPR experiments shown in Figure 6c.

claim: Antigen epitope accessibility can be finely tuned through presentation geometry.
source: These findings demonstrate that antigen epitope accessibility can be finely tuned through presentation geometry, which could be used as a strategy to target the immune response against specific epitopes of interest.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the epitope accessibility experiments comparing different nanoparticle geometries.

claim: De novo designed protein nanoparticles provide a modular way to present antigens to the immune system in defined geometries and of known composition.
source: De novo designed protein nanoparticles provide a modular way to present antigens to the immune system in defined geometries and of known composition.
evidence: This is a summary statement in the Discussion section.

claim: Multivalent antigen presentation can enhance antigen-specific antibody titers by orders of magnitude.
source: Multivalent antigen presentation can enhance antigen-specific antibody titers by orders of magnitude (Bennett et al., 2015; Snapper, 2018), but presentation of complex antigens is challenging due to the required geometric compatibility between antigen and scaffold.
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: The effects of nanoparticle presentation on HIV-1 Env immunogenicity are often modest compared to those observed for other antigens.
source: While previous studies of HIV-1 Env trimers presented on nanoparticle scaffolds have demonstrated enhanced immunogenicity (Escolano et al., 2019), the effects are often modest compared to those observed for other antigens (Bennett et al., 2015; Snapper, 2018; Marcandalli et al., 2019; Brinkkemper and Sliepen, 2019).
evidence: This observation is cited from published literature.

claim: Limitations associated with epitope inaccessibility caused by crowding of the trimers on nanoparticle surfaces have been identified for HIV-1 Env.
source: While there may exist intrinsic peculiarities to HIV-1 Env that limit increases in antibody responses upon multivalent presentation (Klasse et al., 2012; Ringe et al., 2019), limitations associated with epitope inaccessibility caused by crowding of the trimers on nanoparticle surfaces have also been identified (Sanders and Moore, 2017; Brouwer et al., 2019).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: Epitopes proximate to the BG505 SOSIP base were markedly more accessible to immobilized mAbs on BG505 SOSIP–T33_dn2 than BG505 SOSIP–I53-50.
source: Indeed, the SPR experiments presented here demonstrate that epitopes proximate to the BG505 SOSIP base were markedly more accessible to immobilized mAbs on BG505 SOSIP–T33_dn2 than BG505 SOSIP–I53-50, directly implicating steric crowding on the nanoparticle surface as a determinant of antigenicity.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the SPR data in Figure 6.

claim: Steric crowding on the nanoparticle surface is a determinant of antigenicity.
source: Indeed, the SPR experiments presented here demonstrate that epitopes proximate to the BG505 SOSIP base were markedly more accessible to immobilized mAbs on BG505 SOSIP–T33_dn2 than BG505 SOSIP–I53-50, directly implicating steric crowding on the nanoparticle surface as a determinant of antigenicity.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the comparative epitope accessibility data.

claim: The availability of multiple antigen-displaying nanoparticles makes possible the usage of different scaffolds during prime and boost immunizations.
source: Furthermore, the availability of multiple antigen-displaying nanoparticles makes possible the usage of different scaffolds during prime and boost immunizations, which could limit immune responses directed toward the scaffolds while boosting antigen-specific antibody responses.
evidence: This is a proposed application discussed in the Discussion section.

claim: Using different scaffolds during prime and boost immunizations could limit immune responses directed toward the scaffolds while boosting antigen-specific antibody responses.
source: Furthermore, the availability of multiple antigen-displaying nanoparticles makes possible the usage of different scaffolds during prime and boost immunizations, which could limit immune responses directed toward the scaffolds while boosting antigen-specific antibody responses.
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism discussed in the Discussion section.

claim: The ability to tune antigen presentation geometry through de novo nanoparticle design provides a route to investigate the effects of this parameter on B cell activation.
source: Finally, the ability to tune antigen presentation geometry through de novo nanoparticle design provides a route to investigate the effects of this parameter on B cell activation, as well as the potency and breadth of the ensuing humoral response.
evidence: This is a proposed application discussed in the Discussion section.

claim: This design approach could help overcome the intrinsically low affinity of germline BCRs for viral glycoproteins.
source: This design approach could help overcome the intrinsically low affinity of germline BCRs for viral glycoproteins, and enable development of broadly neutralizing antibodies.
evidence: This is a proposed benefit discussed in the Discussion section.

claim: The design approach yields nanoparticles tailored to present 4, 8, or 20 copies of the viral glycoproteins in defined geometries.
source: This design approach yielded nanoparticles tailored to present 4, 8, or 20 copies of the viral glycoproteins in defined geometries (Figure 1d).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1d.

claim: The RPX method identifies configurations likely to accommodate favorable side chain packing at the de novo designed interface.
source: They were docked into C3-symmetric trimers using our RPX docking method, which identifies configurations likely to accommodate favorable side chain packing at the de novo designed interface (Fallas et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a description of the computational method with citation.

claim: Geometrically compatible docks had non-clashing termini separation distances of 15 Å or less.
source: Geometrically compatible docks (non-clashing termini separation distances of 15 Å or less) were subjected to full Rosetta C3-symmetric interface design and filtering (see Materials and Methods), and twenty-three designs were selected for experimental characterization (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a design criterion stated in the Results section.

claim: The designed trimers were derived from three distinct designed helical repeat proteins from TPR, HEAT, or de novo topological families.
source: These four trimers were derived from three distinct designed helical repeat proteins from TPR, HEAT, or de novo topological families (1na0, 3ltj, and HR04, see Materials and Methods) (Brunette et al., 2015; Urvoas et al., 2010; Main et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to the source proteins.

claim: Crystals were obtained for the two designs 1na0C3_2 and 3ltjC3_1v2.
source: Crystals were obtained for the two designs 1na0C3_2 and 3ltjC3_1v2.
evidence: This experimental result is stated in the Results section.

claim: Structures for 1na0C3_2 and 3ltjC3_1v2 were determined at resolutions of 2.6 and 2.3 Å, respectively.
source: Structures were determined at resolutions of 2.6 and 2.3 Å, revealing a backbone root mean square deviation (r.m.s.d.) between the design model and structure of 1.4 and 0.8 Å, respectively (Figure 2—figure supplement 3, and Figure 2—figure supplement 3—source data 1, crystallization conditions, structure metrics, and structure-to-model comparisons are described in Materials and Methods).
evidence: These resolution values are reported from X-ray crystallography.

claim: Most of the atomic details at the de novo designed interfaces are recapitulated in the crystal structures.
source: The structures confirmed in both cases that the designed proteins adopt the intended trimeric configurations, and that most of the atomic details at the de novo designed interfaces are recapitulated.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from comparison of crystal structures to design models.

claim: Three naturally occurring homopentamers were included in the docking calculations to increase the probability of generating icosahedra.
source: To increase the probability of generating icosahedra which confer the highest valency among the targeted symmetries, three naturally occurring homopentamers were also included in the docking calculations (PDB IDs 2JFB, 2OBX, and 2B98).
evidence: This design strategy is stated in the Results section.

claim: Nineteen nanoparticle designs did not form assemblies of the expected size or the resulting assemblies were heterogeneous.
source: SEC chromatograms revealed that nineteen designs did not form assemblies of the expected size or that the resulting assemblies were heterogeneous (Figure 2—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This experimental result is reported with supporting SEC data.

claim: I53_dn5 was selected for in vitro assembly investigation due to its high valency and production yield.
source: Due to its high valency and production yield, we selected the I53_dn5 nanoparticle to investigate the capacity of its two components to be separately produced and assembled in vitro.
evidence: This selection rationale is stated in the Results section.

claim: In vitro assembly confers more control over nanoparticle assembly and composition.
source: In vitro assembly also confers more control over nanoparticle assembly and composition, for example by assembling with a mixture of components fused to different antigens (Boyoglu-Barnum et al., 2020).
evidence: This advantage is stated with a citation to supporting work.

claim: 2,000–5000 particles were manually picked from the electron micrographs acquired for each designed nanoparticle.
source: 2,000–5000 particles were manually picked from the electron micrographs acquired for each designed nanoparticle and classified in 2D using the Iterative MSA/MRA algorithm (see Materials and Methods).
evidence: This is a description of the NS-EM data processing method.

claim: Some free nanoparticle components were detected in the T33_dn5 sample, suggesting a certain propensity towards disassembly.
source: While some free nanoparticle components were detected in the T33_dn5 sample, suggesting a certain propensity towards disassembly, analysis of the reconstructed 3D maps revealed that all five nanoparticles assemble as predicted by the design models, at least to the resolution limits of NS-EM.
evidence: This observation is made from the NS-EM data.

claim: There is less evidence of flexibility in T33_dn10 and O43_dn18 compared to I53_dn5, in agreement with the higher final map resolution for these nanoparticles.
source: There is less evidence of flexibility in T33_dn10 and O43_dn18, in agreement with the higher final map resolution for these nanoparticles.
evidence: This observation is made from the cryo-EM data analysis.

claim: Nanoparticle design models were relaxed into the corresponding EM maps by applying multiple rounds of Rosetta relaxed refinement and manual refinement in Coot.
source: Nanoparticle design models were relaxed into the corresponding EM maps by applying multiple rounds of Rosetta relaxed refinement (Wang et al., 2016) and manual refinement in Coot (Emsley and Crispin, 2018) to generate the final structures.
evidence: This is a description of the structure refinement method.

claim: The refined structures show excellent agreement with the corresponding Rosetta design models.
source: Overall, the refined structures show excellent agreement with the corresponding Rosetta design models.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from comparison of refined cryo-EM structures to design models.

claim: Approximately 500–1000 particles were manually picked from the micrographs for BG505 SOSIP-fused nanoparticle samples.
source: For BG505 SOSIP-fused nanoparticle samples (v5.2 (7S)), approximately 500–1000 particles were manually picked from the micrographs and 2D-classified using the Iterative MSA/MRA algorithm.
evidence: This is a description of the NS-EM data processing method.

claim: The self-assembling cores of the antigen-fused nanoparticles were very similar to the NS-EM maps of the unmodified nanoparticles.
source: The self-assembling cores of the antigen-fused T33_dn2, T33_dn10, and I53_dn5 nanoparticles were very similar to the NS-EM maps of the unmodified nanoparticles (at least to the resolution limits of NS-EM), demonstrating that fusion of the BG505 SOSIP trimer did not induce any major structural changes to the underlying nanoparticle scaffolds.
evidence: This comparison is made from NS-EM reconstructions.

claim: The GG linker connecting DS-Cav1 to I53_dn5 likely accounts for the observed flexibility and suboptimal definition of the glycoprotein trimer in two-dimensional class averages.
source: The GG linker connecting DS-Cav1 to I53_dn5 likely accounts for the observed flexibility and suboptimal definition of the glycoprotein trimer in two-dimensional class averages (Figure 5—figure supplement 1, bottom right).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the NS-EM data.

claim: There was no engineered linker between the glycoprotein and fusion component in the case of HA–I53_dn5.
source: There was no engineered linker between the glycoprotein and fusion component in the case of HA–I53_dn5, and more clearly defined spike density was observed in the class averages (Figure 5—figure supplement 2, bottom right).
evidence: This design feature is stated with reference to the NS-EM data.

claim: More clearly defined spike density was observed in the class averages for HA–I53_dn5 compared to DS-Cav1–I53_dn5.
source: There was no engineered linker between the glycoprotein and fusion component in the case of HA–I53_dn5, and more clearly defined spike density was observed in the class averages (Figure 5—figure supplement 2, bottom right).
evidence: This observation is made from comparison of NS-EM class averages.

claim: D25 is a prefusion specific mAb that binds site Ø of RSV F.
source: D25 is a prefusion specific mAb that binds site Ø (McLellan et al., 2013b).

source: Motavizumab binds site II of the pre and post-fusion conformations (Cingoz, 2009).
evidence: This antibody specificity is cited from published literature.

source: AM14 is trimer-specific binding across protomers of the prefusion conformation (Gilman et al., 2015).
evidence: This antibody specificity is cited from published literature.

claim: Both the HA–I53_dn5 nanoparticle and the HA–I53_dn5B trimer presented the head and stem regions with wild-type-like antigenicity as shown by biolayer interferometry binding experiments.
source: Biolayer interferometry binding experiments with anti-HA head - and stem-specific mAbs (Krause et al., 2011; Ekiert et al., 2009) analogously showed that both the HA–I53_dn5 nanoparticle and the HA–I53_dn5B trimer presented the head and stem regions with wild-type-like antigenicity (Figure 5—figure supplement 2, top).
evidence: This is demonstrated by biolayer interferometry data.

claim: BG505 SOSIP–T33_dn2 was selected to compare against BG505 SOSIP–I53-50 through surface plasmon resonance experiments.
source: We selected the BG505 SOSIP–T33_dn2 tetrahedral nanoparticle (assembled in vitro using BG505 SOSIP–T33_dn2A and T33_dn2B) to compare against a previously published SOSIP-displaying icosahedral nanoparticle (BG505 SOSIP–I53-50) (Brouwer et al., 2019) through surface plasmon resonance (SPR) experiments.
evidence: This experimental design is stated in the Results section.

claim: NS-EM class averages and a 3D reconstruction were generated for BG505 SOSIP–T33_dn2A in complex with the VRC01 Fab, confirming the expected binding mode.
source: To first validate mAb binding to BG505 SOSIP–T33_dn2A, NS-EM class averages and a 3D reconstruction were generated in complex with the VRC01 Fab (Walker et al., 2011), confirming the expected binding mode (Figure 6a).
evidence: This validation is shown in NS-EM data in Figure 6a.

claim: For mAbs that target the more base-proximate epitopes in the gp120-gp41 interface (VRC34 and PGT151), there was nearly three-fold higher epitope accessibility on T33_dn2 compared to I53-50.
source: However, for mAbs that target the more base-proximate epitopes in the gp120-gp41 interface (VRC34 and PGT151), there was nearly three-fold higher epitope accessibility on T33_dn2 compared to I53-50 (Figure 6c).
evidence: This quantitative result is from SPR experiments shown in Figure 6c.

claim: For a mAb that targets the gp41 inter-protomeric epitope (3BC315), no accessibility difference was observed between T33_dn2 and I53-50.
source: Further down the trimer, no accessibility difference was again observed for a mAb that targets the gp41 inter-protomeric epitope (3BC315), which was relatively inaccessible on both nanoparticles, likely due to steric hindrance by neighboring trimers.
evidence: This result is from SPR experiments shown in Figure 6c.

claim: The 3BC315 epitope was relatively inaccessible on both T33_dn2 and I53-50 nanoparticles, likely due to steric hindrance by neighboring trimers.
source: Further down the trimer, no accessibility difference was again observed for a mAb that targets the gp41 inter-protomeric epitope (3BC315), which was relatively inaccessible on both nanoparticles, likely due to steric hindrance by neighboring trimers.
evidence: This interpretation is based on the SPR data and geometric considerations.

claim: The ability to predictively explore new structural space makes designed proteins attractive scaffolds for multivalent antigen presentation.
source: The ability to predictively explore new structural space makes designed proteins (Parmeggiani et al., 2015; Brunette et al., 2015) attractive scaffolds for multivalent antigen presentation.
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citations to designed protein work.

claim: In previous work with computationally designed nanoparticle immunogens, the nanoparticles were generated from naturally occurring oligomeric proteins without initial consideration of geometric compatibility for antigen presentation.
source: In our previous work with computationally designed nanoparticle immunogens (Marcandalli et al., 2019; Brouwer et al., 2019), the nanoparticles were generated from naturally occurring oligomeric proteins without initial consideration of geometric compatibility for antigen presentation.
evidence: This is a description of previous work with citations.

claim: The work demonstrates that antigen-displaying protein nanoparticles can be designed from scratch.
source: This work demonstrates that antigen-displaying protein nanoparticles can be designed from scratch, and provides a systematic way to investigate the influence of antigen presentation geometry on the immune response to vaccination.
evidence: This is a summary statement from the abstract.
